newsitem.title: USA: Tribune sees higher '97 capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Tribune sees higher '97 capital spending.

text.p: Tribune Co expects capital spending in 1997 to total about $135 million, up from $93.3 million last year, the company said in its annual report.

It cited spending for a variety of normal replacement projects as well as for press enhancement and pagination projects at its newspapers and the purchase of digital equipment at its television stations.
Tribune also said it continues to invest in interactive and electronic ventures, though Internet business has yet to show a profit.

It said development losses in the sector were $28 million last year and such losses are expected to decrease to a range of $20 million to $25 million in 1997 "as we generate new revenues that will help offset expenses."
Chairman John Madigan, in a letter to shareholders, said 1997 will usher in mandated stock ownership guidelines of between two and five times salary for nearly 70 of the corporation's top executives.
"We feel this will align the interests of management and shareholders even more closely," Madigan noted.

In 1996, Tribune began offering up to $500 million of its Series D medium-term notes, of which $350 million were issued and outstanding at December 29, 1996. As part of the Series D medium-term note program, the company said it sold $100 million of 6.25 percent notes that mature in 2026.
Tribune said in 1997 it intends to refinance $31.0 million of Series B medium-term notes scheduled to mature this year.
Tribune is a media company involved in newspapers, radio and television broadcasting and educational software.
